About.Name: Dat Thai
About.Currently: Electrical Engineering Student · Power & Energy Systems
About.AboutText:
Hi, I'm Dat Thai, a junior Electrical Engineering student at Seattle Pacific University on the power and energy systems track. I like working on the part of a system everything else depends on: the power. That means batteries, regulators, protection circuits, and the boards that carry them.

Before engineering, I kept buildings running as a building manager and AV technician at UW Bothell, and I now work in facilities at SPU. I also tutored math at Cascadia College. Outside the lab I play soccer and train Brazilian jiu-jitsu.

Experience.ExperienceText: Electrical Engineering student with hands-on experience in power subsystem design, PCB layout in Altium, embedded MicroPython, and analog circuit debugging.
Experience.EducationText: B.S. in Electrical Engineering, power and energy systems track. Transferred from Cascadia College (A.S. in Computer Engineering) with the SPU Transfer Merit Scholarship. Relevant coursework: Electronics I, PCB Design, Microcontroller System Design, Circuits (active filters, Bode analysis), Computer Architecture (MIPS), Electromagnetism, and Junior and Senior Design.
Experience.EmploymentText: Previously Building Manager and AV Technician at the University of Washington Bothell, and Mathematics Tutor at Cascadia College.
Experience.SkillsText: Comfortable taking a circuit from simulation to schematic, layout, and bench testing.

Project1.Title: Peak Detector Circuit
Project1.Desc:
Designed and built a peak detector circuit using op-amps, a diode, and a capacitor to detect the peak voltage of an input signal.

The circuit uses an LM339 comparator to compare the peak detector output against a reference voltage, triggering an LED indicator when the signal exceeds the threshold. Tested and debugged at frequencies ranging from 10kHz to 25kHz.

Project2.Title: Wall-E Warehouse Robot — Power Management Subsystem
Project2.Desc:
Team project (Junior Design). I led the power management subsystem for an autonomous warehouse robot: the LiPo battery, charger, voltage sensor, fuse, motor power switch, and relay circuit.

I built an energy load table across every subsystem to size the battery and fuse, captured the full power schematic in Altium Designer, and presented the subsystem in the faculty design review.

Project3.Title: Dual Adjustable Power Supply PCB
Project3.Desc:
Designed a two-channel adjustable power supply on a 100 × 100 mm board, from schematic capture through PCB layout in Altium Designer.

In PCB Design II, I revised the layout to resolve design-for-manufacturing issues flagged by a PCB fab house.

Project4.Title: Raspberry Pi Pico Embedded Projects
Project4.Desc:
A series of eight MicroPython projects on the Raspberry Pi Pico, simulated in Wokwi and run on hardware.

Covers GPIO interrupts, PWM servo control, shift registers driven from interrupt service routines, SPI LCD output, and file I/O on the Pico's flash.
